dataset: GLDAS Noah v2.1 monthly regional exports
limitations: GLDAS is a modeled hydrological product; these results do not establish crop yield effects or crop damage.
Spatial grid means use complete 0-100 cm profiles and supplied-grid cell areas; they do not apply a Pampas polygon overlap mask.
Newey-West and normal-approximation inference is asymptotic; assess sensitivity to lag choice and analysis period.
Mann-Kendall and Seasonal Kendall p-values do not correct serial autocorrelation.
The full-period climatology is descriptive and should not be used as an issue-time forecast baseline.

methods.0_100_cm_storage: sum SoilMoi0_10cm_inst, SoilMoi10_40cm_inst, SoilMoi40_100cm_inst; all three layers required
methods.anomalies: subtract each calendar month's mean across valid regional observations in the full supplied period
methods.confidence_interval: 95% normal-approximation interval using HAC standard error
methods.mann_kendall: tie-corrected classic test on displayed monthly anomalies plus seasonal Kendall within matching calendar months; both p-values assume independence and are descriptive under serial dependence
methods.regional_trend: OLS trend with calendar-month fixed effects; Newey-West HAC standard error with Bartlett weights and up to 12 calendar-month lags
methods.sen_slope: median of pairwise slopes within matching calendar months, using actual elapsed month indices and scaled to decade
methods.spatial_significance: HAC OLS p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment; cells are spatially dependent, so FDR interpretation is approximate

quality.area_coverage_rule: regional means are withheld below the configured valid-area threshold

spatial_grid.area_weighting: exact spherical regular-grid cell area from latitude bounds
spatial_grid.boundary_rule: all cells in the supplied grid; no polygon overlap fraction applied

spatial_trends_on_cell_seasonal_anomalie.multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment of HAC OLS p-values

units: mm water equivalent (numerically equal to kg m-2)
